📋 Risk-Based Audit Methodology

This audit was conducted following a structured risk-based approach aligned with the COSO Internal Control — Integrated Framework. For each area examined, the audit team: (1) identified applicable risks from the Risk Register, (2) determined the relevant Control Activities designed to mitigate those risks, (3) tested the operating effectiveness of those controls, and (4) documented observations where controls were found to be absent, inadequate, or not consistently applied. Toggle this framework view on any observation card below to see the full Risk Register reference and Control Activity basis for each finding.

Step 1
Risk Identification
Identified applicable risks from the Institutional Risk Register for each audit area.
Step 2
Control Mapping
Mapped relevant Control Activities designed to mitigate each identified risk.
Step 3
Control Testing
Tested operating effectiveness of controls through document review, observation, and inquiry.
Step 4
Observation
Documented deficiencies where controls were absent, inadequate, or inconsistently applied.

Section 1 — Repeated (Unresolved) Observations (31 observations)
#ObservationRiskRef.Detail
1.1 Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts		 M to H BH
🔍 FindingMore specific (micro level) audit findings, along-with recommendations thereon, are as following: Repeated Observations (Un-Resolved) Budgetary limits should be kept in view while making spending. Budgeting and analysis of variances therefrom, are useful monitoring and control tools that can help relevant authorities in the process of effective management and good governance. The review of system generated “Budget Variance Sheets” revealed that overspending was made under certain head of accounts. Few of such instances are shared as Annexure-A.
✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/bank-cash-payment-process/- 3. Branch Operational Budget (Imprest): “Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all Heads of Expenses. System generated budget variance sheet be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancy, if any, rectified. “Branch Purchase Committee and certain analytical reports in the Module e.g. Imprest Budget Variance Statement shall provide support to BH in this regard.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/lfa-esl/ - 6. OPERATIONAL EXPENDITURE: “Monitoring of Opex (Imprest) variances of Branches shall be conducted at RO Finance on monthly basis.”
💬 Auditee ResponseWe will have a vigilant check to monitor the budget variance on monthly basis.
  ↓ Full Obs Card
1.2 Budget for Student Expenditure Remained Unutilized
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingAs per Company policy, savings under the category of student expenses should be avoided. During review of “Budget Variance Sheets”, it was observed that budget for student expenditure remained unutilized in certain heads. Few of such instances are shared as Annexure-B.
✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/bank-cash-payment-process/ - 3. Branch Operational Budget (Imprest): “There should be no saving of funds under the category of ‘student expenses”.
💬 Auditee ResponseWe will have utilized student’s expenditure remaining budget in future.
  ↓ Full Obs Card
1.3 Withholding Tax Deposited with Delay
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts		 M to H BH
🔍 FindingAs per Company policy, tax withheld from suppliers should be deposited within seven days. During review of ledger, delays were observed. Few of the instances are shared as Annexure-C.
✅ RecommendationTax policies should be properly followed, any lapses in this regard may result in penalties to the company. As per SMFO.HO letter dated 04 Jul, 2014: “Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and deposit the same into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment”.
💬 Auditee ResponseWe apologize for late submission of withholding Tax. However, the policy has been implemented with immediate effect. We assure you that this observation will never be repeated again.
  ↓ Full Obs Card
1.4 Reimbursements not Timely Processed by RO
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts		 L to M RO
🔍 FindingBranches are allocated a limited budget for each head of account, and reimbursement claims should be processed in a timely manner. However, based on the detail provided by the branch, delays were observed in the processing of claims. Few of the instances have been shared as Annexure-D.
✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/reimbursement-process/#2--types-of-reimbursable-expenses - 4. Reimbursement Claim Procedure: “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt. SMF-RO and Manager Accounts at HO shall ensure reconciliation of inter office reimbursements balances on monthly basis”.
💬 RO ResponsePlease be informed that ROC Finance handles branch reimbursement cases in a systematic manner, prioritizing them among other tasks. As a result, 20-day completion timeline is not consistently achievable. Below are a few factors that cause deviations from the 20-day timeline. Some bills are based on purchase orders (POs) and are forwarded to the relevant departments (Procurement, Marketing, Construction) for PO generation, which takes additional processing time. Certain bills are received late from branches due to delays in completing the related activities and engagement in urgent tasks. Sometimes, priority items at desk is another factor of late processing the claims. Furthermore, in practical scenarios, the 20-day timeline is often insufficient for the majority of cases.
👁 Audit ViewThe number of days is mentioned in the policy. However, any changes required in this regard may be properly documented as feedback and coordinated for necessary updation (if applicable). As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/33-exceptions-amendments/ - 32. Exceptions & Amendments: “Any amendments and revisions to the Manual as deemed necessary shall be incorporated as per SOP no. S&A/SOP/003 for “Development and Amendment of Policies & Procedures”. (Extract from SOP no. S&A/SOP/003 ) As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/SOP-003-Final-pdf-5th-Nov-24.pdf: “4.2.2 Proposals for revisions/amendments of policies shall be discussed between Department Head / authorized representatives (Process Owner) and S&A team along with necessary explanations and justifications. 4.2.3 The Head S&A and Department Head shall evaluate the submitted proposal in the context of control requirements and objectives of the Organization.”
  ↓ Full Obs Card

Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingFor balance confirmation purposes, the Branch was requested for the balance confirmation certificates from the vendors with whom the business activities were done and staff to whom advances were issued (during the audit period). 1.7 Vendors Registration not Performed
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts		 M to H BH
🔍 FindingAs per policy, procurement shall be made from registered vendors. The registered vendor is a vendor for which Vendor Master Data is available in Vendor Register for Branches, based on approved VRF. However, the practice of vendor registration was not being properly followed, and the vendor register was not maintained.
✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/procurement/sourcing-selection-registration-of-vendors/2/ - 2. Registration of Vendors: “The procurement shall be made from registered vendors. The registered vendor is a vendor for which Vendor Master Data is created ….. in Vendor Register for Branches based on approved VRF. The designated …. BPC shall complete the VRF, based on the criteria detailed above and sign the completed form. VRF and related documents, if any, shall be forwarded to Senior ….. BH for approval. …. BH shall review the documents submitted and provide approval on VRF for inclusion in Vendor ….. Register, upon satisfaction.”
💬 Auditee ResponseVendor registration is in process now. We will ensure strict compliance in future.
  ↓ Full Obs Card
1.8 Employees Record of Social Security not Available
Recruitment, Payroll & Employee Record		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingAs per Punjab Govt directions, employees having salary from Rs. 41,000 (or as prescribed by the notification issued time to time) should be registered with Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (providing hospitalization and dispensary facilities etc.) It was observed that PESSI record for the payments etc., was not available.
✅ RecommendationAppropriate procedure should be devised and adopted at concerned levels regarding; Registration of employees. PESSI record. keeping (for instance PESSI Employee Cards). Monthly payment. Employees should also be informed about the benefits provided by PESSI for example medical care facilities and cash benefits to the secured workers and their dependents.
💬 Auditee ResponseRegistration of employees was recorded in the files as a copy of PESSI Card and was also presented on request. We did not have rights to access monthly payment record of emplyees. However Head Office was contacted for the guidance so that require data can be fetched from Beams and maintain at school level too.
👁 Audit ViewIt is requested that the branch should be facilitated in this regard, so that the same may be referred, whenever required.
  ↓ Full Obs Card

Recruitment, Payroll & Employee Record		 M to H BH
🔍 FindingAttendance should be properly marked by all employees. As per BEAMS record, it was noted that outgoing attendance was not marked in certain cases. Due to the issue, compliance of office timings cannot be verified. The matter may affect also their Leave Encashment. Few of the instances has been shared in Annexure-F.
✅ RecommendationBranch Management should monitor attendance record of the branch employees. Moreover, in case of out attendance not marked, staff should raise application for the attendance not marked, or early leaving (whichever is applicable) highlighting the reasons. As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/16-working-hours-attendance-2/2/#3--attendance - 3. Attendance: “Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices.
💬 Auditee ResponseStrict follow up will be ensured in future. In past we used be more vigilantly following up time in by referring to the attendance calendar of habitual late comers. However in future same practice will be adopted to monitor time out of all those who do not apply it on daily basis.

✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/14-clearance-final-settlement-2/ - 5. Timeline: “Keeping in view all the requirements, the clearance and final settlement process must not take more than three working weeks barring exceptions.”
💬 Auditee ResponseWe will ensure strict compliance for follow up of final settlement claims in future. ROC is also requested to finalize claims at their earliest.
💬 RO ResponseThe final settlement process through BEAMS has significantly enhanced efficiency, reducing turnaround times. However, delays in final settlements persist, particularly from July to October, primarily due to delays in profit calculations at the Corporate Finance end. Additionally, the online issuance of cheques—which takes over 2-3 weeks at the signatories end—further contributes to the delays. Instances of employees going on uninformed absences, long leaves, or not serving their notice period also result in delays, as resignation order/ end-of-employment issuances are processed based on their last working day. Furthermore, positions such as Librarian, and OFA that require proper handover processes tend to experience additional delays in the settlement process.

1.18 Un-Numbered Assets
Fixed Assets		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingFixed assets codes should be affixed on all assets. It was observed during physical verification of assets that fixed assets codes were not affixed on some assets of the branch. Few of the instances are mentioned below: [Sr. No. | Description | Qty | Location
1 | Steel Bench | 21 | Ground
2 | Height & Weight Machine | 01 | UPS Store]
✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/acquisition-of-fixed-assets/#3--coding-of-fixed-assets - 3. Coding of Fixed Assets: “Each fixed asset would be assigned unique identification number (Code) at the time of its acquisition.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/acquisition-of-fixed-assets/#3--coding-of-fixed-assets - 3. Coding of Fixed Assets: “Following Officials shall affix codes on respective fixed assets within 15 days of receipt of fixed assets codes:” [Office/Branch | Coding Responsibility
Branch | AMCO/ BA (in case of no Caretaker) (with the help of Technical & Support Staff)] As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/physical-verification-of-fixed-assets/ - Un-numbered Assets: “List of untraced assets, manual GRNs and transfer notes may be reviewed to identify assets to whom codes may have not been assigned yet. The reviewing authority as mentioned in Clause ‎6.2.7 may recommend adjustment of “unnumbered asset” against untraced asset keeping in view the specification and acquisition date of that untraced asset. The format to note is attached as FAM-H Unnumbered Assets.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/physical-verification-of-fixed-assets/ - 2. Procedure for Verification: “Findings of physical verification shall be arranged into following categories: Duplicate assets – Two or more assets having same code. Un-matched assets – Coded asset physically present but not appearing in the list. Un-numbered assets – Assets without codes.”
💬 Auditee ResponseThe observation is noted. The responsibility for tagging fixed assets lies with the Branch OFA. The asset codes were not affixed on some assets due to oversight. The Branch OFA has now been instructed to ensure that asset codes are properly affixed on all assets. Compliance will be ensured going forward through regular verification to avoid recurrence of such observations.

2.1 Significant Anomalies in Processing of Paint Bills
Branch Imprest, Payments& Accounts		 M to H BH
🔍 FindingDuring the audit, it was observed that paint bills were processed without proper verification of measurements claimed by paint contractor and related deductions. Few of such discrepancies included: Glass affixed in doors was not deducted from the painted area. White boards installed on the walls were also not properly deducted from the painted area. For example, in the branch some of the whiteboards were affixed partially on surfaces painted with emulsion and partially on surfaces painted with enamel. However, the deductions were not made in accordance with the applicable paint type (i.e. emulsion or enamel)/rate. As informed by Branch Personnel: Verification of the paint material by minimum two members of the Purchase Committee (PC) was not conducted to ensure that the supplied material complied with the approved specifications. The paint brand and quality were also not verified by AMCO, prior to application. The paint bills were processed without verification by AMCO. Signed delivery challans were not available to verify documentation regarding the receipt of materials. No documentary evidence was available to verify that approval had been obtained for the application of the second coat after completion of the first, as required under the prescribed process. Verification of the application of double coats was not carried out by the Admin and Accounts. Weather Shield was applied in certain areas before the prescribed period (of three years); however, no exception approval from the competent authority was obtained for the early reapplication. Paint Brand was not mentioned on the bills, and quotations.
✅ RecommendationPaint bills should be properly checked prior to processing. All measurements should be verified before processing of paint bills. Any excess amount identified should be recovered from the vendor. Deductions for glass panels, white boards, and other non-painted areas should be properly done. Paint brand, quality, and material receipt should be verified before and during application. Necessary approvals and supporting documents should be maintained to verify the compliance of prescribed policies and procedures.
💬 Auditee ResponseStrict compliance in future.
👁 Audit ViewDuring re-verification of paint bills by the branch an amount of appr. Rs. 30,000 was identified as paid in excess. As per email from Mr. Hussain Farooq (hussainfarooq.55130@bh.edu.pk), dated Apr 30, 2026: “PFA scanned copies of Annual Paint Bill measurements difference after Audit team guidance, we rechecked the actual measurements of annual paint bill and verified by our AMCO. The difference amount of Year 2023, 2024 and 2025 recoverable from Paint Vendor as under:

2.10 Significant Anomalies in Bake Sales Record
Cash & Bank		 High BH
🔍 FindingDuring the audit, significant non-compliance with prescribed policies and deficiencies in documentation related to Bake Sale activities were identified. These included: Detail of Bake Sales was not properly maintained. Bake Sale Activity for 2022 was still open in “Cash Collection Module”, and there was no record available. For the year 2025 & 2026: Committee formation details for Bake Sale activities were not available. Serial Number Receipt Book record was not available. Detailed cash collection record was not available for verification, including (but not limited to): Collections, donations, and the balances etc. Compliance with price ceiling of PKR 200 per item. Compliance with student cash limit of PKR 500 per student. Activities were not recorded in “Cash Collection Module”. Approval from BH (after closure of activity) was not available. Receipt for Rs. 50,000 donated to SKMT (Year 2025) was not available. Balances from Bake Sale e.g. Rs. 2,420 (Feb 2025), and Rs. 20,710 (Jan 2026) were not recorded in module.
✅ RecommendationCompany policies should be followed and the record should be properly maintained. As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/events/bake-sale/4/ - Administration of Cash Collection: “The school must devise ways to administer the cash collected during the bake sale. The school head is responsible to make committees for the collection of cash which should be properly documented. The branch accountant should not be part of the said committee. The committee should stay mobile throughout the event for cash management. The committee should use a serially numbered receipt book for the purpose of cash collection from the students. The collected cash should be handed over to the branch accountant who would ensure its proper recording in the cash collection module as well as maintenance of manual memorandum record as per the cash collection policy. In-house set-up is suggested to hold the bake sale. In case any expense is carried out for the set-up purpose e.g. tentage, tables etc., such expenses, however, will not be loaded on the Branch imprest. The expense will be adjusted from the cash collected from the students. In summation, the cash to be handed over to the charity will be net-off such expenses. The branch accountant should submit the activity account at the closure of the activity to the School Head for her/ his approval and closure of the activity thereafter. The school management must take students on board as to who the recipients of this charity are. The school may conduct an assembly and invite the recipients and/or send the student representatives over with the charity. Bake Sale Guidelines for Beaconhouse.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/events/bake-sale/2/ - 5. Rules and Procedures: “Communication: Schools must set up a cash limit for the students attending the bake sale as an audience. Cash per student may be limited to PKR 500 for the bake sale donation drive. Price Ceiling: School must establish a price limit for the items on sale. Cost per item should not exceed PKR 200. In order to serve umpteem in a restricted cost bracket the item size can be aligned.” Due to unavailability of record and the highlighted issues, the cash collection from Bake Sales could not be verified. There is need to complete the record on urgent basis, and submit in RO for checking.
💬 Auditee ResponseWe will strictly follow the polices and balance amount of both years Bake Sale will be deposited in Taare Zameen par trust.

2.43 Discrepancies with Library Module (KOHA)
Library		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingEfficient utilization of library software (KOHA) should be ensured. Proper trainings and proper rights of the library module (KOHA) should also be provided to the librarians to ensure this. Certain discrepancies were observed and subsequently confirmed by the branch librarian in discussion which seemed to be creating difficulties for the librarians in performing their day to day operations regarding library module. Such as: For branch librarian rights to view & access books were not restricted to specific branch. Auto generation of Over-due books notification (email) was not in practice. Auto generation of Issued & Returned books notification (email) was not in practice. Stocktaking through bar codes and subsequently stocktaking report generation.
✅ RecommendationKeeping in view the importance of above mentioned features which are already available in existing open source library module (KOHA), there is a need to ensure to access and practice of these options for the more controlled, efficient, accurate and scrutinized working of branch librarians by utilizing the available resources.
💬 Auditee ResponseThe discrepancies noted regarding the KOHA library module are acknowledged. The Librarian will coordinate with the Regional Office to restrict librarian access to their respective branches, implement stocktaking using barcodes, and activate auto-generation of notifications for overdue, issued, and returned books. These measures will ensure more controlled, efficient, and accurate use of the library module.

✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/memorandum-registers-at-branch/ - 4. Other Stock Registers: “Following Stock Registers shall also be maintained by the Branch. Laboratory Equipment Register” [Sr. No. | Stock Register | Maintained BY | Checked By BH
1 | Laboratory Equipment | Laboratory Incharge | Monthly] As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/memorandum-registers-at-branch/#2--science--general-laboratory-registers - 2. Science / General Laboratory Registers: Laboratory stock registers should be maintained separately for all labs i.e. Biology, Chemistry, Physics & General Science. Consumption / Practical register should be maintained for all labs on daily basis.”
💬 Auditee ResponseThe Laboratory Attendant acknowledges the discrepancies noted in the Science Laboratory Stock Register. The Laboratory Equipment Register will be maintained and checked monthly as per policy.

2.46 Fuel Average Monitoring not Properly Conducted
Others		 M to H BH
🔍 FindingThe OFA/AO is responsible for calculating fuel average of generator. Manager Admin Regional Office (RO) should also ensure timely communication of the generator’s standard fuel average to the Branch. During the audit it was observed that OFA was not properly monitoring the generator’s fuel consumption. The Regional Office had also not communicated the standard fuel average. As informed by the OFA: Fuel balance was mentioned on assumption. They were not checking the actual balance. Opening balance of fuel (on month start), and closing balance of fuel (on month end) was not accounted for during calculation of fuel consumption. This may lead to untracked variances in fuel efficiency.
✅ RecommendationAs per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/construction-renovation-maintenance/generator-repair-hiring/ - 2. Record Keeping (Logbook): “OFA/AO shall be informed about the standard fuel average of the genset by the relevant Manager Admin RO. OFA/AO shall calculate the fuel average of the generator on the basis of entries recorded in the logbook, after regular intervals (preferable at the time of new fueling). Fuel Average = Fuel Consumption ÷ Running Hours”
💬 Auditee ResponseThe observation is noted. The OFA was maintaining records as per previous practice. However, the branch does not have the equipment to verify the generator’s exit fuel average. As per the audit recommendation, the branch will ensure that records are maintained in accordance with the policy and coordinate with the RO to receive the standard fuel average for proper monitoring. Going forward, the branch will implement all feasible measures to track fuel consumption accurately within the available resources.”
  ↓ Full Obs Card
2.47 Stock Register not Maintained for Used Engine Oil
Others		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingDuring the audit, it was observed that the Stock Register for used Engine Oil was not maintained. No proper record was available regarding the quantity of used mobile oil received after oil change of generator, stored, or disposed.
✅ RecommendationThe stock register may be maintained, preferable in a standardized format for such stock maintaining. As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/memorandum-registers-at-branch/ 6. Memorandum Registers at Branch: “For the purpose of effective control, certain stock registers shall be maintained by Branches. Standard “Stock Registers” containing columns for receipt, issuance, balance and remarks shall be used for this purpose.”
💬 Auditee ResponseThe observation is noted. The OFA was not aware of the policy regarding used mobile oil. Following guidance from the audit team, the branch will now ensure full compliance by maintaining proper records of used mobile oil, including its generation, storage, and disposal, in accordance with the policy.
  ↓ Full Obs Card
2.48 Inward Gate Pass not in Practice
Others		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingGate Passes are the basic tool for controlling the inward /outward movement of items. However, during review it was observed that the practice for preparing inward gate pass was not implemented.
✅ RecommendationAs per standard practice, gate pass should be implemented to ensure efficient monitoring control over movement, and future reference for evidence of receipt of assets.
💬 Auditee ResponseThe observation is noted. The OFA acknowledges that the inward gate pass practice was not previously implemented. To address this, the branch has now introduced the use of an Asset Return Stamp for recording and verifying the return of assets. Going forward, this process will be strictly followed to ensure proper documentation and control over asset movements in compliance with policy.
  ↓ Full Obs Card
2.49 Incomplete List of Photocopier & Canteen Contractor Assets
Others		 L to M BH
🔍 FindingDuring the audit, lists of photocopier, and the canteen contractor assets were found unsigned by the concerned parties, and the date on which assets were recorded/checked was also not mentioned.
✅ RecommendationAs per standard practice, it is recommended that the detail of photocopier, and canteen contractor assets duly signed by both parties of the contract, should be kept in the branch to differentiate the assets of company and assets of photocopier and canteen contractor.
💬 Auditee ResponseList of Photocopier Assets now signed by School Head. Evidence shared. List of Canteen Assets completed but was not signed by School Head. Now singed by School Head. Evidence shared. Action Taken As confirmed above, the lists were signed. Follow Up All relevant Authorities are requested to inform us of the action taken with respect to the issues raised. 📋 Detailed Observations — Section 1: Repeated
1.1 Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount M to H 🔁 Repeated BH
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 1.1
Risk Register Reference
RR-FIN-01
Financial Mismanagement Risk
Risk of non-compliance with financial policies, improper budgetary controls, and delayed payments leading to financial losses or regulatory penalties.
Likelihood: Medium Impact: High Inherent Risk: High Residual Risk: Medium-High Risk Appetite: Low
Control Objective: Ensure all financial transactions are authorized, accurately recorded, and comply with Company financial policies and statutory requirements.
Control Activity Applied
CA-FIN-01
Budget Variance Monitoring Control
Monthly review of budget variance reports by Branch Head and ROC Finance to ensure expenditure remains within approved budgetary limits across all heads of accounts.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Budget Variance Monitoring Control against Financial Mismanagement Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
More specific (micro level) audit findings, along-with recommendations thereon, are as following: Repeated Observations (Un-Resolved) Budgetary limits should be kept in view while making spending. Budgeting and analysis of variances therefrom, are useful monitoring and control tools that can help relevant authorities in the process of effective management and good governance. The review of system generated “Budget Variance Sheets” revealed that overspending was made under certain head of accounts. Few of such instances are shared as Annexure-A.
✅ Recommendation▼
As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/bank-cash-payment-process/- 3. Branch Operational Budget (Imprest): “Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all Heads of Expenses. System generated budget variance sheet be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancy, if any, rectified. “Branch Purchase Committee and certain analytical reports in the Module e.g. Imprest Budget Variance Statement shall provide support to BH in this regard.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/lfa-esl/ - 6. OPERATIONAL EXPENDITURE: “Monitoring of Opex (Imprest) variances of Branches shall be conducted at RO Finance on monthly basis.”
💬 Auditee Response▼
We will have a vigilant check to monitor the budget variance on monthly basis.
↑ Back to Synopsis

1.3 Withholding Tax Deposited with Delay M to H 🔁 Repeated BH
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 1.3
Risk Register Reference
RR-FIN-01
Financial Mismanagement Risk
Risk of non-compliance with financial policies, improper budgetary controls, and delayed payments leading to financial losses or regulatory penalties.

Control Objective: Ensure all financial transactions are authorized, accurately recorded, and comply with Company financial policies and statutory requirements.
Control Activity Applied
CA-FIN-02
Tax Compliance Control
Verification that withholding tax deductions are deposited within the statutory 7-day period and properly recorded in financial records.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Tax Compliance Control against Financial Mismanagement Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
As per Company policy, tax withheld from suppliers should be deposited within seven days. During review of ledger, delays were observed. Few of the instances are shared as Annexure-C.
✅ Recommendation▼
Tax policies should be properly followed, any lapses in this regard may result in penalties to the company. As per SMFO.HO letter dated 04 Jul, 2014: “Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and deposit the same into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment”.
💬 Auditee Response▼
We apologize for late submission of withholding Tax. However, the policy has been implemented with immediate effect. We assure you that this observation will never be repeated again.

1.4 Reimbursements not Timely Processed by RO L to M 🔁 Repeated RO
Branch Imprest, Payments & Accounts
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 1.4
Risk Register Reference
RR-FIN-01
Financial Mismanagement Risk
Risk of non-compliance with financial policies, improper budgetary controls, and delayed payments leading to financial losses or regulatory penalties.
Likelihood: Low Impact: Medium Inherent Risk: Medium Residual Risk: Low-Medium Risk Appetite: Moderate
Control Objective: Ensure all financial transactions are authorized, accurately recorded, and comply with Company financial policies and statutory requirements.
Control Activity Applied
CA-FIN-03
Claims Processing & Authorization Control
Review and timely processing of reimbursement claims within the 20-day policy timeline with proper authorization at RO Finance level.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Claims Processing & Authorization Control against Financial Mismanagement Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
Branches are allocated a limited budget for each head of account, and reimbursement claims should be processed in a timely manner. However, based on the detail provided by the branch, delays were observed in the processing of claims. Few of the instances have been shared as Annexure-D.
✅ Recommendation▼
As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/reimbursement-process/#2--types-of-reimbursable-expenses - 4. Reimbursement Claim Procedure: “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt. SMF-RO and Manager Accounts at HO shall ensure reconciliation of inter office reimbursements balances on monthly basis”.
💬 RO Response▼
Please be informed that ROC Finance handles branch reimbursement cases in a systematic manner, prioritizing them among other tasks. As a result, 20-day completion timeline is not consistently achievable. Below are a few factors that cause deviations from the 20-day timeline. Some bills are based on purchase orders (POs) and are forwarded to the relevant departments (Procurement, Marketing, Construction) for PO generation, which takes additional processing time. Certain bills are received late from branches due to delays in completing the related activities and engagement in urgent tasks. Sometimes, priority items at desk is another factor of late processing the claims. Furthermore, in practical scenarios, the 20-day timeline is often insufficient for the majority of cases.
👁 Audit View▼
The number of days is mentioned in the policy. However, any changes required in this regard may be properly documented as feedback and coordinated for necessary updation (if applicable). As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/33-exceptions-amendments/ - 32. Exceptions & Amendments: “Any amendments and revisions to the Manual as deemed necessary shall be incorporated as per SOP no. S&A/SOP/003 for “Development and Amendment of Policies & Procedures”. (Extract from SOP no. S&A/SOP/003 ) As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/wp-content/uploads/2024/11/SOP-003-Final-pdf-5th-Nov-24.pdf: “4.2.2 Proposals for revisions/amendments of policies shall be discussed between Department Head / authorized representatives (Process Owner) and S&A team along with necessary explanations and justifications. 4.2.3 The Head S&A and Department Head shall evaluate the submitted proposal in the context of control requirements and objectives of the Organization.”
↑ Back to Synopsis

1.8 Employees Record of Social Security not Available L to M 🔁 Repeated BH
Recruitment, Payroll & Employee Record
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 1.8
Risk Register Reference
RR-HR-01
Human Resource Compliance Risk
Risk of non-compliance with HR policies regarding recruitment, payroll processing, employee confirmation, and record maintenance.
Likelihood: Low Impact: Medium Inherent Risk: Medium Residual Risk: Low-Medium Risk Appetite: Moderate
Control Objective: Ensure HR processes are conducted in accordance with Company policy, statutory requirements, and employee entitlements are accurately processed.
Control Activity Applied
CA-SEC-01
Security Arrangement Compliance Control
Verification of security personnel credentials and compliance with contractual obligations, including the requirement for 50% ex-armed forces personnel.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Security Arrangement Compliance Control against Human Resource Compliance Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
As per Punjab Govt directions, employees having salary from Rs. 41,000 (or as prescribed by the notification issued time to time) should be registered with Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (providing hospitalization and dispensary facilities etc.) It was observed that PESSI record for the payments etc., was not available.
✅ Recommendation▼
Appropriate procedure should be devised and adopted at concerned levels regarding; Registration of employees. PESSI record. keeping (for instance PESSI Employee Cards). Monthly payment. Employees should also be informed about the benefits provided by PESSI for example medical care facilities and cash benefits to the secured workers and their dependents.
💬 Auditee Response▼
Registration of employees was recorded in the files as a copy of PESSI Card and was also presented on request. We did not have rights to access monthly payment record of emplyees. However Head Office was contacted for the guidance so that require data can be fetched from Beams and maintain at school level too.
👁 Audit View▼
It is requested that the branch should be facilitated in this regard, so that the same may be referred, whenever required.

1.10 Outgoing Attendance not Marked by Staff M to H 🔁 Repeated BH
Recruitment, Payroll & Employee Record
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 1.10
Risk Register Reference
RR-HR-01
Human Resource Compliance Risk
Risk of non-compliance with HR policies regarding recruitment, payroll processing, employee confirmation, and record maintenance.
Likelihood: Medium Impact: High Inherent Risk: High Residual Risk: Medium-High Risk Appetite: Low
Control Objective: Ensure HR processes are conducted in accordance with Company policy, statutory requirements, and employee entitlements are accurately processed.
Control Activity Applied
CA-HR-01
Attendance & Time Management Control
Regular monitoring of employee attendance records through BEAMS to ensure compliance with prescribed office hours and proper marking of arrival and departure.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Attendance & Time Management Control against Human Resource Compliance Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
Attendance should be properly marked by all employees. As per BEAMS record, it was noted that outgoing attendance was not marked in certain cases. Due to the issue, compliance of office timings cannot be verified. The matter may affect also their Leave Encashment. Few of the instances has been shared in Annexure-F.
✅ Recommendation▼
Branch Management should monitor attendance record of the branch employees. Moreover, in case of out attendance not marked, staff should raise application for the attendance not marked, or early leaving (whichever is applicable) highlighting the reasons. As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/16-working-hours-attendance-2/2/#3--attendance - 3. Attendance: “Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices.
💬 Auditee Response▼

💬 Auditee Response▼
We will ensure strict compliance for follow up of final settlement claims in future. ROC is also requested to finalize claims at their earliest.
💬 RO Response▼
The final settlement process through BEAMS has significantly enhanced efficiency, reducing turnaround times. However, delays in final settlements persist, particularly from July to October, primarily due to delays in profit calculations at the Corporate Finance end. Additionally, the online issuance of cheques—which takes over 2-3 weeks at the signatories end—further contributes to the delays. Instances of employees going on uninformed absences, long leaves, or not serving their notice period also result in delays, as resignation order/ end-of-employment issuances are processed based on their last working day. Furthermore, positions such as Librarian, and OFA that require proper handover processes tend to experience additional delays in the settlement process.

Risk Register Reference
RR-OPS-01
Asset Management & Safeguarding Risk

Control Activity Applied
CA-OPS-01
Fixed Asset Verification & Recording Control
Physical verification of fixed assets against the Fixed Asset Register to ensure all assets are properly numbered, recorded, and any discrepancies are investigated and resolved.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Fixed Asset Verification & Recording Control against Asset Management & Safeguarding Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
Fixed assets codes should be affixed on all assets. It was observed during physical verification of assets that fixed assets codes were not affixed on some assets of the branch. Few of the instances are mentioned below: [Sr. No. | Description | Qty | Location
1 | Steel Bench | 21 | Ground
2 | Height & Weight Machine | 01 | UPS Store]
✅ Recommendation▼
As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/acquisition-of-fixed-assets/#3--coding-of-fixed-assets - 3. Coding of Fixed Assets: “Each fixed asset would be assigned unique identification number (Code) at the time of its acquisition.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/acquisition-of-fixed-assets/#3--coding-of-fixed-assets - 3. Coding of Fixed Assets: “Following Officials shall affix codes on respective fixed assets within 15 days of receipt of fixed assets codes:” [Office/Branch | Coding Responsibility
Branch | AMCO/ BA (in case of no Caretaker) (with the help of Technical & Support Staff)] As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/physical-verification-of-fixed-assets/ - Un-numbered Assets: “List of untraced assets, manual GRNs and transfer notes may be reviewed to identify assets to whom codes may have not been assigned yet. The reviewing authority as mentioned in Clause ‎6.2.7 may recommend adjustment of “unnumbered asset” against untraced asset keeping in view the specification and acquisition date of that untraced asset. The format to note is attached as FAM-H Unnumbered Assets.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/fixed-assets/physical-verification-of-fixed-assets/ - 2. Procedure for Verification: “Findings of physical verification shall be arranged into following categories: Duplicate assets – Two or more assets having same code. Un-matched assets – Coded asset physically present but not appearing in the list. Un-numbered assets – Assets without codes.”
💬 Auditee Response▼
The observation is noted. The responsibility for tagging fixed assets lies with the Branch OFA. The asset codes were not affixed on some assets due to oversight. The Branch OFA has now been instructed to ensure that asset codes are properly affixed on all assets. Compliance will be ensured going forward through regular verification to avoid recurrence of such observations.

2.1 Significant Anomalies in Processing of Paint Bills M to H 🆕 New BH
Branch Imprest, Payments& Accounts
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 2.1
Risk Register Reference
RR-FIN-01
Financial Mismanagement Risk
Risk of non-compliance with financial policies, improper budgetary controls, and delayed payments leading to financial losses or regulatory penalties.
Likelihood: Medium Impact: High Inherent Risk: High Residual Risk: Medium-High Risk Appetite: Low
Control Objective: Ensure all financial transactions are authorized, accurately recorded, and comply with Company financial policies and statutory requirements.
Control Activity Applied
CA-OPS-06
General Operational Compliance Control
Review of operational records and procedures to ensure compliance with applicable Company policies and standard operating procedures.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of General Operational Compliance Control against Financial Mismanagement Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
During the audit, it was observed that paint bills were processed without proper verification of measurements claimed by paint contractor and related deductions. Few of such discrepancies included: Glass affixed in doors was not deducted from the painted area. White boards installed on the walls were also not properly deducted from the painted area. For example, in the branch some of the whiteboards were affixed partially on surfaces painted with emulsion and partially on surfaces painted with enamel. However, the deductions were not made in accordance with the applicable paint type (i.e. emulsion or enamel)/rate. As informed by Branch Personnel: Verification of the paint material by minimum two members of the Purchase Committee (PC) was not conducted to ensure that the supplied material complied with the approved specifications. The paint brand and quality were also not verified by AMCO, prior to application. The paint bills were processed without verification by AMCO. Signed delivery challans were not available to verify documentation regarding the receipt of materials. No documentary evidence was available to verify that approval had been obtained for the application of the second coat after completion of the first, as required under the prescribed process. Verification of the application of double coats was not carried out by the Admin and Accounts. Weather Shield was applied in certain areas before the prescribed period (of three years); however, no exception approval from the competent authority was obtained for the early reapplication. Paint Brand was not mentioned on the bills, and quotations.
✅ Recommendation▼
Paint bills should be properly checked prior to processing. All measurements should be verified before processing of paint bills. Any excess amount identified should be recovered from the vendor. Deductions for glass panels, white boards, and other non-painted areas should be properly done. Paint brand, quality, and material receipt should be verified before and during application. Necessary approvals and supporting documents should be maintained to verify the compliance of prescribed policies and procedures.
💬 Auditee Response▼
Strict compliance in future.
👁 Audit View▼
During re-verification of paint bills by the branch an amount of appr. Rs. 30,000 was identified as paid in excess. As per email from Mr. Hussain Farooq (hussainfarooq.55130@bh.edu.pk), dated Apr 30, 2026: “PFA scanned copies of Annual Paint Bill measurements difference after Audit team guidance, we rechecked the actual measurements of annual paint bill and verified by our AMCO. The difference amount of Year 2023, 2024 and 2025 recoverable from Paint Vendor as under:

General Operational Compliance Control
Review of operational records and procedures to ensure compliance with applicable Company policies and standard operating procedures.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of General Operational Compliance Control against Cash & Bank Integrity Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
During the audit, significant non-compliance with prescribed policies and deficiencies in documentation related to Bake Sale activities were identified. These included: Detail of Bake Sales was not properly maintained. Bake Sale Activity for 2022 was still open in “Cash Collection Module”, and there was no record available. For the year 2025 & 2026: Committee formation details for Bake Sale activities were not available. Serial Number Receipt Book record was not available. Detailed cash collection record was not available for verification, including (but not limited to): Collections, donations, and the balances etc. Compliance with price ceiling of PKR 200 per item. Compliance with student cash limit of PKR 500 per student. Activities were not recorded in “Cash Collection Module”. Approval from BH (after closure of activity) was not available. Receipt for Rs. 50,000 donated to SKMT (Year 2025) was not available. Balances from Bake Sale e.g. Rs. 2,420 (Feb 2025), and Rs. 20,710 (Jan 2026) were not recorded in module.
✅ Recommendation▼
Company policies should be followed and the record should be properly maintained. As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/events/bake-sale/4/ - Administration of Cash Collection: “The school must devise ways to administer the cash collected during the bake sale. The school head is responsible to make committees for the collection of cash which should be properly documented. The branch accountant should not be part of the said committee. The committee should stay mobile throughout the event for cash management. The committee should use a serially numbered receipt book for the purpose of cash collection from the students. The collected cash should be handed over to the branch accountant who would ensure its proper recording in the cash collection module as well as maintenance of manual memorandum record as per the cash collection policy. In-house set-up is suggested to hold the bake sale. In case any expense is carried out for the set-up purpose e.g. tentage, tables etc., such expenses, however, will not be loaded on the Branch imprest. The expense will be adjusted from the cash collected from the students. In summation, the cash to be handed over to the charity will be net-off such expenses. The branch accountant should submit the activity account at the closure of the activity to the School Head for her/ his approval and closure of the activity thereafter. The school management must take students on board as to who the recipients of this charity are. The school may conduct an assembly and invite the recipients and/or send the student representatives over with the charity. Bake Sale Guidelines for Beaconhouse.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/events/bake-sale/2/ - 5. Rules and Procedures: “Communication: Schools must set up a cash limit for the students attending the bake sale as an audience. Cash per student may be limited to PKR 500 for the bake sale donation drive. Price Ceiling: School must establish a price limit for the items on sale. Cost per item should not exceed PKR 200. In order to serve umpteem in a restricted cost bracket the item size can be aligned.” Due to unavailability of record and the highlighted issues, the cash collection from Bake Sales could not be verified. There is need to complete the record on urgent basis, and submit in RO for checking.
💬 Auditee Response▼
We will strictly follow the polices and balance amount of both years Bake Sale will be deposited in Taare Zameen par trust.

2.30 Security Refund Report not Generated from ISM/BEAMS L to M 🆕 New RO
Student Record
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 2.30
Risk Register Reference
RR-OPS-03
Student Data Integrity Risk
Risk of incomplete, inaccurate, or improperly maintained student records leading to regulatory non-compliance and operational issues.
Likelihood: Low Impact: Medium Inherent Risk: Medium Residual Risk: Low-Medium Risk Appetite: Moderate
Control Objective: Ensure student records are complete, accurately maintained in BEAMS, and accessible only to authorized personnel.
Control Activity Applied
CA-SEC-01
Security Arrangement Compliance Control
Verification of security personnel credentials and compliance with contractual obligations, including the requirement for 50% ex-armed forces personnel.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Security Arrangement Compliance Control against Student Data Integrity Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
Efficient utilization of ISM/BEAMS should be ensured. Proper access rights and training should also be provided in this regard. Additionally, the IT department may be contacted to request the generation of specific additional reports as needed. It was observed that for branch PROs, no intimation, report, or pop-up is generated (branch-wise) through ISM/BEAMS, for the preparation and dispatch of students' security refund cheques. A sample format for such a report is provided below:
✅ Recommendation▼
Keeping in view the importance of above mentioned report (branch wise), there is a need to ensure the availability of this report. option (with view rights only) for more effective working of branch PROs.
💬 Auditee Response▼
Noted for future compliance.
💬 RO Response▼
Security refund is being dealt centrally at RO Level and all the reports are maintained and monitored at RO Level. However, the PROs have the rights of Quick view to see the details against Cheque preparation and dispatch information.
👁 Audit View▼
In our opinion, such report may be provided to the branch for their support.
↑ Back to Synopsis
2.31 Aspects of Assets not Mentioned in Fixed Asset Register L to M 🆕 New RO
Fixed Assets
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 2.31
Risk Register Reference
RR-OPS-01
Asset Management & Safeguarding Risk
Risk of misappropriation, loss, or inaccurate recording of fixed assets leading to financial misstatement or operational disruption.
Likelihood: Low Impact: Medium Inherent Risk: Medium Residual Risk: Low-Medium Risk Appetite: Moderate
Control Objective: Ensure all fixed assets are properly recorded, physically tagged, periodically verified, and disposed of through approved procedures.
Control Activity Applied
CA-OPS-01
Fixed Asset Verification & Recording Control
Physical verification of fixed assets against the Fixed Asset Register to ensure all assets are properly numbered, recorded, and any discrepancies are investigated and resolved.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Fixed Asset Verification & Recording Control against Asset Management & Safeguarding Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
Aspect of assets (Brand, Make, Model etc.) should be mentioned in fixed asset register. It was observed during physical verification and scrutiny of fixed asset record, that only category of assets was mentioned, aspects containing description of the assets were not available in fixed asset register of the branch.
✅ Recommendation▼
For authentic physical verification of assets, including Brand, Make, Model, and other relevant details, it is necessary that the same information be accurately recorded in the branch’s Fixed Assets Register.
💬 Auditee Response▼
Noted for future compliance.
💬 RO Response▼
Noted for compliance. Additionally, in recent years assets additions, brand / model is mentioned in fixed assets register.
↑ Back to Synopsis

2.33 Delay in Return of Books by Students M to H 🆕 New BH
Library
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 2.33
Risk Register Reference
RR-OPS-02
Educational Resource Management Risk
Risk of inadequate library resource management, non-compliance with library policies, and improper use of library management systems.
Likelihood: Medium Impact: High Inherent Risk: High Residual Risk: Medium-High Risk Appetite: Low
Control Objective: Ensure library resources are adequately maintained, properly catalogued in the library management system, and utilized effectively for educational purposes.
Control Activity Applied
CA-OPS-03
Library Resource Management Control
Periodic review of library records, book inventory, KOHA module compliance, and librarian meeting documentation to ensure effective library management.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Library Resource Management Control against Educational Resource Management Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
Books should be returned within stipulated time. It was observed during the audit that books were not returned within stipulated time by students. Few of such instances are mentioned as Annexure-J.
✅ Recommendation▼
As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/library-manuals-2/9-koha-and-lending-resources/ - Book Issuance: “A library book may be issued for a maximum period of two weeks at a time. Renewals may be permitted based on availability.”
💬 Auditee Response▼
The observation is acknowledged. Students will be reminded to return books within the stipulated two-week period as per the library policy, and the library staff will monitor the return process more closely to ensure timely compliance.
↑ Back to Synopsis

2.35 Dispose Books Still Appearing in Library Module L to M 🆕 New BH
Library
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 2.35
Risk Register Reference
RR-OPS-02
Educational Resource Management Risk
Risk of inadequate library resource management, non-compliance with library policies, and improper use of library management systems.
Likelihood: Low Impact: Medium Inherent Risk: Medium Residual Risk: Low-Medium Risk Appetite: Moderate
Control Objective: Ensure library resources are adequately maintained, properly catalogued in the library management system, and utilized effectively for educational purposes.
Control Activity Applied
CA-OPS-03
Library Resource Management Control
Periodic review of library records, book inventory, KOHA module compliance, and librarian meeting documentation to ensure effective library management.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Library Resource Management Control against Educational Resource Management Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
The Library Module should be updated on timely basis. Disposal of books should be processed in module immediately upon approval of AIDN by RO. During audit we found that many books were appearing in library module but physically not available in the branch. On further inquiry, it was observed that, these books have been disposed-off but their disposal was not yet processed in Library Module. Few of such instances are mentioned as Annexure-L.
✅ Recommendation▼
To ensure accuracy and efficiency, the Library Module should be updated on a regular basis. Book disposals should be entered into the module promptly after receiving approval from RO. As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/library-manuals-2/14-weeding-the-school-library-collection/ - 14. Weeding the School Library Collection: “Procedure for the disposal notes: Dispose-off the outdated and damaged resources and make disposal notes and get approval through School Head if “Teaching Aid Category”/ or through the Regional office if “Main Category”. Referred to Branch
💬 Auditee Response▼
The observation is acknowledged. The books were disposed-off after approval; however, their disposal was not updated in the Library Module timely. The record will be updated accordingly, and the library staff will ensure that all future disposals are entered in the module promptly after RO approval to maintain accurate records.
💬 RO Response▼
Librarians are instructed to promptly update record on KOHA.

2.43 Discrepancies with Library Module (KOHA) L to M 🆕 New BH
Library
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 2.43
Risk Register Reference
RR-OPS-02
Educational Resource Management Risk
Risk of inadequate library resource management, non-compliance with library policies, and improper use of library management systems.
Likelihood: Low Impact: Medium Inherent Risk: Medium Residual Risk: Low-Medium Risk Appetite: Moderate
Control Objective: Ensure library resources are adequately maintained, properly catalogued in the library management system, and utilized effectively for educational purposes.
Control Activity Applied
CA-OPS-03
Library Resource Management Control
Periodic review of library records, book inventory, KOHA module compliance, and librarian meeting documentation to ensure effective library management.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of Library Resource Management Control against Educational Resource Management Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
Efficient utilization of library software (KOHA) should be ensured. Proper trainings and proper rights of the library module (KOHA) should also be provided to the librarians to ensure this. Certain discrepancies were observed and subsequently confirmed by the branch librarian in discussion which seemed to be creating difficulties for the librarians in performing their day to day operations regarding library module. Such as: For branch librarian rights to view & access books were not restricted to specific branch. Auto generation of Over-due books notification (email) was not in practice. Auto generation of Issued & Returned books notification (email) was not in practice. Stocktaking through bar codes and subsequently stocktaking report generation.
✅ Recommendation▼
Keeping in view the importance of above mentioned features which are already available in existing open source library module (KOHA), there is a need to ensure to access and practice of these options for the more controlled, efficient, accurate and scrutinized working of branch librarians by utilizing the available resources.
💬 Auditee Response▼
The discrepancies noted regarding the KOHA library module are acknowledged. The Librarian will coordinate with the Regional Office to restrict librarian access to their respective branches, implement stocktaking using barcodes, and activate auto-generation of notifications for overdue, issued, and returned books. These measures will ensure more controlled, efficient, and accurate use of the library module.

2.46 Fuel Average Monitoring not Properly Conducted M to H 🆕 New BH
Others
📋 Risk-Based Audit Framework — 2.46
Risk Register Reference
RR-OPS-05
General Operational Compliance Risk
Risk of non-compliance with operational policies and procedures covering miscellaneous branch activities.
Likelihood: Medium Impact: High Inherent Risk: High Residual Risk: Medium-High Risk Appetite: Low
Control Objective: Ensure all operational activities are conducted in accordance with Company policies and procedures.
Control Activity Applied
CA-OPS-06
General Operational Compliance Control
Review of operational records and procedures to ensure compliance with applicable Company policies and standard operating procedures.
Audit Conclusion: Based on the application of General Operational Compliance Control against General Operational Compliance Risk, the following observation was identified during the audit.
🔍 Finding / Observation▼
The OFA/AO is responsible for calculating fuel average of generator. Manager Admin Regional Office (RO) should also ensure timely communication of the generator’s standard fuel average to the Branch. During the audit it was observed that OFA was not properly monitoring the generator’s fuel consumption. The Regional Office had also not communicated the standard fuel average. As informed by the OFA: Fuel balance was mentioned on assumption. They were not checking the actual balance. Opening balance of fuel (on month start), and closing balance of fuel (on month end) was not accounted for during calculation of fuel consumption. This may lead to untracked variances in fuel efficiency.
✅ Recommendation▼
As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/construction-renovation-maintenance/generator-repair-hiring/ - 2. Record Keeping (Logbook): “OFA/AO shall be informed about the standard fuel average of the genset by the relevant Manager Admin RO. OFA/AO shall calculate the fuel average of the generator on the basis of entries recorded in the logbook, after regular intervals (preferable at the time of new fueling). Fuel Average = Fuel Consumption ÷ Running Hours”
💬 Auditee Response▼
The observation is noted. The OFA was maintaining records as per previous practice. However, the branch does not have the equipment to verify the generator’s exit fuel average. As per the audit recommendation, the branch will ensure that records are maintained in accordance with the policy and coordinate with the RO to receive the standard fuel average for proper monitoring. Going forward, the branch will implement all feasible measures to track fuel consumption accurately within the available resources.”
↑ Back to Synopsis
